questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. Its area is:
questions.rationale: Semi-perimeter s = 21; area = sqrt(21 x 8 x 7 x 6) = sqrt(7056) = 84 sq cm (Heron's formula).

questions.question: The area of an equilateral triangle of side 8 cm is:
questions.rationale: Area = (root 3 / 4) x side^2 = (root 3 / 4) x 64 = 16 root 3, about 27.71 sq cm. Option 64 root 3 forgets to divide by 4.

questions.question: The length of a rectangle is three times its breadth and its perimeter is 96 m. Its area is:
questions.rationale: 2(l + b) = 96 so l + b = 48 and with l = 3b, b = 12, l = 36. Area = 36 x 12 = 432 sq m.

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus measure 24 cm and 10 cm. The side of the rhombus is:
questions.rationale: Diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so side = sqrt(12^2 + 5^2) = 13 cm. Its area would be (24 x 10)/2 = 120 sq cm.

questions.question: A trapezium has parallel sides of 18 cm and 12 cm and the distance between them is 8 cm. Its area is:
questions.rationale: Area = half x (sum of parallel sides) x height = 0.5 x 30 x 8 = 120 sq cm. Forgetting the half gives 240.

questions.question: The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. Taking pi = 22/7, its area is:
questions.rationale: 2 x (22/7) x r = 44 gives r = 7 cm. Area = (22/7) x 49 = 154 sq cm. 308 is the circumference formula with an extra factor of 2 applied to the area.

questions.question: A sector of a circle has radius 21 cm and a central angle of 60 degrees. Taking pi = 22/7, its area is:
A rectangular lawn measures 40 m by 30 m. A path 2 m wide runs around it on the outside. The area of the path is:
questions.rationale: Outer rectangle = 44 x 34 = 1496 sq m; lawn = 1200 sq m; path = 296 sq m. Shortcut: 2 x 2 x (40 + 30 + 2 x 2) = 296.

questions.question: A ring is bounded by two concentric circles with radii 14 cm and 7 cm. Taking pi = 22/7, its area is:
questions.rationale: Area = pi (R^2 - r^2) = (22/7)(196 - 49) = 462 sq cm. Using (R - r)^2 would be the usual slip.

questions.question: The diagonal of a square is 20 cm. Its area is:
questions.rationale: Area of a square = (diagonal^2)/2 = 400/2 = 200 sq cm.

questions.question: A rectangular field is 150 m long and 90 m wide. The cost of fencing it all round at Rs 12 per metre is:
questions.rationale: Perimeter = 2(150 + 90) = 480 m; cost = 480 x 12 = Rs 5,760. Using the area instead of the perimeter would be wrong because fencing runs along the boundary only.

questions.question: The length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and its breadth is decreased by 10%. The area changes by:
questions.rationale: New area = 1.2 x 0.9 = 1.08 of the old, a rise of 8%. Never add 20 and subtract 10; the changes multiply.

questions.question: The radius of a circle is increased by 10%. The area of the circle increases by:
questions.rationale: Area goes as radius squared: 1.1^2 = 1.21, so the increase is 21%. Doubling 10% to 20% ignores the extra 1% from the cross term.

questions.question: Taking pi = 22/7, the perimeter of a semicircle of radius 14 cm (including the diameter) is:
questions.rationale: Curved part = pi r = 44 cm; add the diameter 28 cm. Perimeter = 72 cm. Quoting only 44 cm leaves out the straight edge.

questions.question: A wheel has a diameter of 70 cm. Taking pi = 22/7, how many complete revolutions does it make to cover 1.76 km?
questions.rationale: Circumference = (22/7) x 70 = 220 cm. Distance = 1.76 km = 176000 cm. Revolutions = 176000/220 = 800.
